title: Windowed Flow-Control Canary with Dependency Safeguards and Amortized Ramp
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a release-window-aware canary controller with amortized traffic ramps and dependency-aware rollback triggers. Improves safety for late-night and peak-hour rollouts; configurable metrics-based rollback thresholds.
description:
Summary: Adds a new windowed flow-control canary controller that ramps traffic only during configured release windows, amortizes increases across multiple windows, and performs dependency-aware prechecks and automated rollback. Motivation: We still see regressions when simple timeouts or sudden ramp-ups coincide with downstream cold starts or dependent service incidents. This controller reduces blast radius by only increasing cohorts during low-risk windows and by validating downstream dependencies (KV cache warm, schema checks, healthy upstreams) before advancing.

What this PR changes: single controller and operator flow, new release window CRD extension, a lightweight dependency health probe framework, telemetry hooks (per-window SLO snapshots), and a small e2e job for the amortized ramp behavior. The controller implements a composite rollback policy that combines service-level indicators (p95 latency, 5xx rate), user-facing quality metrics (eval set regression delta), and dependency health gates.

Design and behavior (high level): - Release windows: operator config accepts a list of windows (day-of-week, start/end UTC, optional timezone override). Ramps are only advanced if the current time falls within an allowed window. - Amortized ramp: instead of doubling traffic in one window, the controller spreads increases across N windows (configurable, default N=3) to smooth capacity needs and observe drifting signals. - Dependency safeguards: before each ramp step the controller runs dependency prechecks (kv_warm: bool, upstream_schema_ok: bool, feature_flag_consistency: bool). If any precheck fails, the canary enters 'quarantine' where traffic is held and periodic rechecks are scheduled. - Composite rollback: triggers when any of the following are true within a window: p95 latency increases > 40% vs baseline, 5xx error rate > 1.5%, eval set regression > 2% absolute, or a dependent service health check flips to unhealthy. Rollbacks are immediate and include a short cool-down lock to avoid flapping. - A/B support: the controller understands cohort mappings and will pause other A/B arms while an amortized ramp is in flight if configured.

Commits (summary): - feat(canary): add window parsing, ramp scheduler, and state machine (Maya Chen) - feat(health): add dependency health probe library with adapter hooks for KV and upstream APIs (Maya Chen) - test(e2e): add amortized ramp e2e harness and CI job (Maya Chen)

Files changed (high level): - pkg/controller/canary/windowed_controller.go (core controller state machine and scheduler) - api/v1alpha/releasewindow_types.go (CRD fields for windows and amortization) - internal/health/probes/kv_probe.go (KV warm probe adapter) - internal/health/probes/upstream_probe.go (upstream schema/health checks) - docs/rollouts/windowed_canary.md (operator docs + examples) - test/e2e/windowed_amortized_ramp_test.go (harness) - charts/redwood/templates/canary-controller.yaml (helm values for windows)

Small config snippet (example release window in YAML):
apiVersion: rollouts.redwood.ai/v1alpha1
kind: ReleaseWindow
metadata:
  name: low-traffic-evening
spec:
  windows:
    - day: "Mon-Fri"
      start: "22:00"
      end: "03:00"
      timezone: "UTC"
  amortizeAcrossWindows: 3
  dependencyGuards:
    - kv_warm
    - upstream_schema_ok

Testing and CI: Initial CI run showed lint failures (unused var in upstream_probe) and one flaky e2e related to a timing assumption; fixes were pushed in commit 3 and CI passed on re-run. Checks: unit (pass), lint (pass after fix), e2e (pass on rerun), integration-sanity (pass).

Review thread (highlights): - Samir Patel: "Overall design looks good. Two asks: make the 40%/1.5%/2% thresholds config-driven (not hardcoded) and add telemetry labels to indicate which window caused the rollback so SRE can filter incident noise." - Maya Chen (author): "Thanks Samir — thresholds and telemetry labels are now configurable via the CRD and emitted as canary.window_id in metrics. Updated in commit 2." - Evelyn Ross: "Can we add unit tests that simulate a failing dependency probe and ensure quarantine behavior doesn't accidentally block other independent canaries?" - Maya Chen: "Added a focused test in test/e2e/windowed_amortized_ramp_test.go and a small mock harness to validate quarantine scoping. See commit 3." - Lars Berg: "CI flaky test noted earlier — once green I'm fine with merging." - Lars Berg (approve): "LGTM"

CI annotations: - initial run: unit: pass, lint: fail (fixed), e2e: flaky (timing), integration-sanity: pending - rerun: all checks passing

Deployment notes and rollback plan: This feature is behind a feature flag (canary.windowed.enabled = false by default). To enable: flip the feature flag in helm and apply a ReleaseWindow CR. Rollout should be tested first in staging with amortizeAcrossWindows=1 then gradually increase. Rollback: operator supports immediate revert and a 15-minute cooldown lock to prevent thrash.

Related tickets and context: ENG-2148 (release window MVP), ENG-2201 (dependency probe framework). This PR unblocks scheduled night-time releases and reduces peak-hour regressions.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after CI green and approvals. Commit message: "windowed canary: amortized ramp + dependency guards (ENG-2148, ENG-2201)".

Notes for docs team: docs/rollouts/windowed_canary.md contains examples and should be incorporated into the rollout playbook.

Contact: @maya.chen for follow-ups and handover to SRE for alerting thresholds.
